interface.title: micromorph - SEM morphology analysis (v0.1)
interface.field: materials science / electron microscopy (fibrous materials, nonwovens, electrospun mats)
interface.stage_of_work: image analysis and quantification after SEM imaging
interface.what_it_is_for: Segment an SEM image of a fiber network with Otsu thresholding, correct dark fiber-center bands wrongly marked as pores by reclassifying regions on shape, and report fiber diameter and void/pore chord-length distributions (d50/p95) that can be exported as CSV or HTML.

data.note: I uploaded A0_Ax1000.tif at magnification x1000, then replaced it with A0_Ax5000.tif at x5000. The uploader holds one file: adding a second file replaced the first. I did not use the x200, x500 or x2000 test files. Pixel calibration comes from the magnification dropdown (Hitachi S-4800 defaults: 0.0990 µm/px at x1000, 0.0200 at x5000, 0.4960 at x200).

features.name: Preset-or-custom shape classifier with live diagnostic overlay
features.general: Sort candidate background regions into 'actually object', 'true background' and 'unsure' using shape thresholds. Pick a named strictness preset or tune the thresholds yourself, see the classes colour-coded on the image with counts, and get a warning when too much is unsure.
features.specific: In Step 2, press Default / Aggressive / Conservative / Custom, or drag the pseudo_pore aspect_ratio_min, solidity_min, circularity_max and noise filter sliders. Red/blue/yellow overlay and pseudo_pore / real_void / ambiguous / noise / flipped-area metrics update. An 'Ambiguous regions account for X% … consider manual QC' warning appears above 5% ambiguous area; otherwise 'No diagnostic warnings'.
steps: Pick a quick preset (Default, Aggressive or Conservative)
Read the counts and the flipped-area percentage beside the overlay
Drag a threshold slider; the label switches to Custom with a 'values don't match any preset' note
Read the diagnostic warning (or 'No diagnostic warnings')
Press a preset again to reset the sliders
serves_tasks: Find background regions that are really parts of the object and flip them, at a chosen strictness
Compare the mask before and after correction and see which regions changed

features.name: Before/after mask comparison with change highlight
features.general: Show the original and corrected binary masks side by side with their area fractions and the difference, then highlight the changed regions on the raw image. Toggling the correction on or off shows how much it moves the downstream numbers.
features.specific: Step 3 shows Initial mask (v1) and Revised mask (v2) with fiber area fraction (+pp) and a green 'Flipped regions' overlay with region count. Step 4 repeats Fiber area v1 (raw) vs v2 (refined). The Enable shape reclassification checkbox turns the correction off; the size of the shift depends on the classifier settings in use.
steps: Look at v1 and v2 masks side by side
Read both fiber area fractions and the +pp change
Inspect the green flipped regions on the raw image
Untick Enable shape reclassification to see v2 = v1 and the uncorrected d50/p95
serves_tasks: Compare the mask before and after correction and see which regions changed
Run without the correction to see how much it matters

features.name: Contour overlay for segmentation QC
features.general: Draw segmentation outlines over the raw image to check alignment. Choose which phase to outline (auto-chosen from coverage, foreground or background), hide small regions with a minimum-area filter, and turn the overlay off to compare with the bare image. If outlines miss, go back and retune the correction.
features.specific: Final edge confirmation: Show contours toggle, Contour mode radio (Auto, which picks void outlines at high fiber coverage / Fiber boundaries / Void boundaries), Minimum region area to display slider (20–500 px), and a caption giving how many boundaries were drawn. This changes the display only, not the measurements.
steps: Leave Contour mode on Auto or pick Fiber or Void boundaries
Drag Minimum region area to display to hide small regions
Read the 'Drawn N … boundaries (area > X px)' caption
Toggle Show contours off to see the raw image
If outlines do not sit on the fibers, return to Step 2 and change preset or sliders
serves_tasks: Overlay segmentation outlines on the raw image and inspect them, going back to the correction step if they do not line up

features.name: Distribution summary with interactive histogram + CDF
features.general: Summarise a measured size population as median and 95th percentile with n, and plot it as a histogram and a cumulative curve with hover and zoom.
features.specific: Step 4 shows Fiber diameter and Void (Pore) chord length d50/p95/n metrics and Plotly histograms and CDFs (hover, box zoom, double-click reset).
steps: Read d50, p95 and n for each distribution
Hover a histogram bar for its bin range and count
Drag a box on the CDF to zoom, then double-click to reset
serves_tasks: Read size distributions and summary percentiles

features.name: Three-file results export (summary row, raw values, report)
features.general: Export one analysis as a one-row summary table, a long table of every measured value, and a readable HTML report, so results can be compared or re-analysed elsewhere.
features.specific: Step 4 Download results.csv (one row with um_per_px, d50/p95 for fiber diameter, void chord and MIC pore diameter), distributions.csv (metric,value_um rows, including *_mic_diameter_um) and report.html (summary table). Each export holds one image.
steps: Press Download results.csv for the summary row
Press Download distributions.csv for every measured value
Press Download report.html for the summary table as a page
serves_tasks: Download results as tables and a report
Analyse a second image at its own scale and export its results

features.name: Sample-type mode switch with interpretation caveat
features.general: Declare whether the sample is a single layer or a stacked 3D network. The tool renames background measurements (void vs pore) and warns that, for stacked samples, apparent void sizes are upper bounds to cross-check with a bulk method.
features.specific: Morphology buttons Fiber network (stacked 3D) / (2D single layer) switch labels real_void ↔ real_pore and Void ↔ Pore chord length without changing numbers. Stacked 3D shows a Step 4 note that void metrics are upper bounds (check against MIP or microCT). Only these two modes work in v0.1.
steps: Press Fiber network (stacked 3D) or (2D single layer)
Check the Step 2 and Step 4 labels (void or pore)
Read the Step 4 interpretation note before reporting void/pore sizes
serves_tasks: Pick the structure model that matches the sample
Tell the analysis whether the sample is one layer or stacked layers, so pore metrics are read correctly

features.name: Magnification-driven calibration
features.general: Choose the instrument magnification so pixels convert to physical units. The calibration and the scale-dependent processing (closing radius) follow from that choice.
features.specific: The Magnification dropdown (x200–x5000) sets µm/px from Hitachi S-4800 defaults, shown in Step 1 with the closing radius. Design gap: there is no check against the image, so a wrong choice (x200 on an x5000 image) breaks the mask with no warning, and there is no custom µm/px entry.
steps: Upload the image
Pick its magnification in the dropdown
Check Calibration and Closing radius in Step 1
Check the Step 1 mask looks sane, since no mismatch warning is given
serves_tasks: Load the image and give its scale
Analyse a second image at its own scale and export its results
Check that the scale setting matches the image, because a wrong one breaks the analysis without warning
